record.paper_title: Current Open Questions in Complete Mixability
record.original_question: Suppose a distribution F satisfies a known sufficient condition for n-complete mixability, such as one of the conditions listed earlier in Section 2.2. Is there a way to simulate samples from an n-complete mix with margins F?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 9. Suppose that F satisfies one of the sufficient conditions (for instance, (b) in Section 2.2) and hence is n-CM. Could we simulate sample from a n-complete mix with margins F?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A distribution function $F$ on $\mathbb{R}$ is called $n$-completely mixable ($n$-CM) if there exist random variables $X_1, \dots, X_n$, each with marginal distribution $F$, such that
$$X_1 + X_2 + \cdots + X_n = n\,\mu_F \quad \text{almost surely},$$
for some constant $\mu_F \in \mathbb{R}$ (necessarily equal to the mean of $F$ when it exists). A random vector $(X_1,\dots,X_n)$ realizing this property is called an $n$-complete mix with margins $F$.

Several sufficient conditions for $n$-complete mixability are known. For example, if $F$ has a monotone density on its (bounded) support and the mean satisfies an appropriate moderate-mean condition, then $F$ is $n$-CM; other sufficient conditions involve symmetry/unimodality assumptions.

Problem: Suppose $F$ is known to satisfy such a sufficient condition guaranteeing that $F$ is $n$-CM. Provide an explicit, implementable algorithm that produces samples from a joint distribution $(X_1, \dots, X_n)$ whose marginals are all equal to $F$ and whose coordinates sum almost surely to the constant $n\,\mu_F$ — that is, design a simulation procedure for an $n$-complete mix with margins $F$.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a definitive algorithm or published solution for general simulation of an n-complete mix with arbitrary margins F satisfying standard sufficient conditions for n-complete mixability. Existing literature on complete mixability focuses on existence results, detection, and convex minimization, rather than constructive simulation. The status appears unresolved in general, though partial constructions may exist for specific subclasses (e.g., monotone densities); evidence is inconclusive.

status_evidence.title: The complete mixability and convex minimization problems with monotone marginal densities
status_evidence.snippet: Distributions with monotone density and moderate mean are completely mixable; results address existence and minimization, not explicit simulation.
status_evidence.claim: Sufficient conditions for n-CM are established but explicit simulation procedures are not the focus.

status_evidence.title: Detecting complete and joint mixability
status_evidence.snippet: Detection of complete and joint mixability via convergence rates of the minimal variance problem.
status_evidence.claim: Related work addresses detection rather than direct simulation of complete mixes.
